current.title: Teen Vaping Crashed 72%. Nicotine Found A New Door.
current.hook: The vaping crisis didn't end. It just moved.
current.closing: One nicotine habit down, a stealthier one clocked in.
current.question: Do you know anyone who vapes or uses pouches? Tell me below.

segments.say: In 2011, just 1.5 percent of high schoolers vaped. By 2017 it was 11.7 percent. By 2019, 27.5 percent -- more than one in four teenagers using e-cigarettes regularly.
Then came flavor bans and FDA crackdowns on Juul. Vaping crashed from 27.5 percent at its peak to just 7.8 percent by 2024 -- the lowest in a decade.

segments.topic: which nicotine product teens use now
segments.say: But e-cigarettes are still nicotine's top seller among teens -- now trailed by nicotine pouches at 1.8 percent, barely regulated. Same habit, quieter: tucked in a lip instead of a cloud.

held_for: judge: Five beats of the same four numbers drawn as charts, with Data standing on top of the labels he is covering — the crash never becomes a picture.

judge.one_line: Five beats of the same four numbers drawn as charts, with Data standing on top of the labels he is covering — the crash never becomes a picture.
problems: hook@0.3 is a blank gradient with a title card: no motion, no image, no reason to stay through the first second.
The mascot occludes data in four separate scenes — "7.8%" at seg3:mid, "27.5%" at seg2:start, the title at seg2:mid, the 2011 bar at seg1:end.
seg0 and seg1 are the identical dataset twice: columns, then rows. The second telling adds nothing.
seg3:end is a near-empty frame — one small film-strip bar bottom-left and two grey stubs under a completely dead upper two-thirds.
Data never performs a bit: he perches, points, and slides to a new mark; for the last five seconds he stands motionless at the foot of a finished bar.
The 2011-2019 rise and the 2019-2024 crash are told with the same generic grammar, so the story's turn ("it just moved") never registers visually.
fixes: Replace the hook with a full-bleed subject image in motion at t=0: a dense cloud of 27.5% arriving and collapsing to 7.8% in under a second, title entering over it, not before it.
Collision-test mascot placement against every label and title bounding box; offset him outward when he overlaps — no value or heading may sit under the character.
Cut one of seg0/seg1. Spend the reclaimed seconds making the 2019 peak arrive with weight instead of restating it as rows.
Make the crash a bespoke mechanic made of the subject: a vapour column whose volume drains 27.5 -> 7.8 while a pouch slides in under the lip and holds a small, stubborn 1.8.
Give Data one real bit with a setup -> action -> payoff: he plugs the vape cloud shut, turns to celebrate, and the pouch appears behind him — tied to the actual numbers.
Extend the final beat's motion (pouch settling, count ticking) or trim it by 2s so the video ends on movement instead of a held frame.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
